name: US campaign against Venezuela and 'narco-terrorist' groups (Operation Southern Spear)
started: 2025-09-02 (first lethal strike on a boat in the Caribbean)
summary: Since September 2025 the United States has waged a lethal air and naval campaign against small boats it says carry drugs for designated 'narco-terrorist' groups, killing about 238 people in 79 strikes by early October 2026, according to InSight Crime. On 3 January 2026 a raid on Caracas captured Nicolás Maduro, and the acting government that replaced him now cooperates with Washington. The boat strikes continue, mostly in the eastern Pacific.

sides.name: United States
members: US Southern Command and Joint Task Force Southern Spear (headquarters at Naval Station Mayport, Florida)
US Navy: USS Gerald R. Ford carrier strike group (Caribbean, Nov 2025 to Feb 2026), USS Iwo Jima amphibious group with the 22nd Marine Expeditionary Unit
US Air Force, Marine Corps and Air National Guard aircraft (F-22, F-35A/C, F/A-18E/F, EA-18G, B-1B, B-52, AC-130J, P-8A)
1st Special Forces Operational Detachment-Delta (Delta Force) and 160th Special Operations Aviation Regiment
CIA, FBI Hostage Rescue Team, DEA, US Coast Guard
backers: Dominican Republic (access to San Isidro air base and Las Americas airport from 26 Nov 2025)
Trinidad and Tobago (radar site and airport access)
El Salvador (hosted AC-130J, P-8A and C-40 aircraft)
leaders: Pete Hegseth (Secretary of Defense, styled Secretary of War)
Gen. Dan Caine (Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff)
sides.strength: About 15,000 personnel at the peak of the build-up, with a carrier, 6 destroyers, a cruiser, 3 amphibious ships and a nuclear submarine (Wikipedia, Operation Southern Spear, accessed Oct 2026)

sides.name: Maduro government (until 3 Jan 2026)
members: Cuban military and intelligence personnel guarding Maduro
sides.strength: Not estimated in the sources consulted

sides.name: Targeted trafficking networks
members: Crews of alleged drug boats and semi-submersibles in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific
Cartel de los Soles (designated a terrorist organization by the US in Nov 2025)
leaders: 'Niño Guerrero' (Tren de Aragua leader, killed in a US strike in June 2026)
sides.strength: Unknown; strikes typically kill two to six people per boat

background: In 2025 the Trump administration began treating Latin American drug trafficking groups as terrorist organizations and military targets. On 2 October 2025 it told Congress that the US was in a 'non-international armed conflict' with designated cartels, whose members it called 'unlawful combatants', and that drug smuggling amounted to an 'armed attack' on the US. Congress has passed no authorization for this use of force, and former government lawyers and rights groups say the strikes amount to extrajudicial killings, while the White House says it acts within the law of armed conflict. This matters because it is the legal basis for every strike in the campaign, and it is being tested in lawsuits and an Inspector General review.

At the same time the US assembled its largest naval force in the Caribbean in decades, aimed at the government of Nicolás Maduro, which Washington accused of running the 'Cartel de los Soles'. The USS Gerald R. Ford carrier group arrived in mid-November 2025, F-35s and electronic-warfare jets moved to Puerto Rico, and access deals were struck with the Dominican Republic, Trinidad and Tobago and El Salvador.
year: The campaign began with a strike off Venezuela on 2 September 2025 that killed 11 people; the administration later confirmed a follow-up strike that killed two survivors. From late October 2025 the strikes spread to the eastern Pacific, which became the main theatre. In December 2025 the US designated the Clan del Golfo a terrorist organization, declared fentanyl a weapon of mass destruction, began seizing oil tankers and announced its first strike on land, a CIA drone attack on a Venezuelan port with no reported casualties.

On 3 January 2026, Operation Absolute Resolve sent more than 150 aircraft from 20 bases against air defences and military sites around Caracas while Delta Force, flown in by 160th SOAR helicopters, seized Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores at Fuerte Tiuna. They were flown via the USS Iwo Jima to New York, where they pleaded not guilty to narco-terrorism charges. Cuba said 32 of its personnel died; Venezuela's defence minister counted 47 Venezuelan military dead; US officials estimated about 75 deaths in total. Seven US troops were wounded and none killed.

Vice President Delcy Rodríguez became acting president, restored relations with Washington (embassy reopened 30 March), opened the oil sector and released hundreds of political prisoners under an amnesty law. The Ford left for the Middle East in February 2026. In June 2026 a US strike, coordinated with Venezuelan intelligence, killed Tren de Aragua leader 'Niño Guerrero'. Boat strikes continued through the year: the death toll reached at least 199 by late May 2026 and 238 in 79 strikes by 5 October 2026, when a Caribbean strike killed four people.
situation: As of late October 2026 the boat strikes continue at a lower tempo than their late-2025 peak, with two deadly strikes and seven non-lethal ones in September 2026 and a lethal Caribbean strike on 4 October. Venezuela is no longer an adversary: the interim government of Delcy Rodríguez shares intelligence with the US, and she promised elections at the UN in September 2026 but set no date. Maduro awaits trial in New York. The large naval build-up has ended, but the legal claim of an armed conflict with cartels remains in force and is now applied across the region, including joint strikes in Ecuador.
technical: Legal basis: 2 Oct 2025 notice to Congress declaring a 'non-international armed conflict' with designated cartels; no Authorization for Use of Military Force covers the strikes (CBS News; Al Jazeera).
Strike count: 79 strikes and 238 dead by 5 Oct 2026 per InSight Crime (includes non-lethal strikes); AP-based count of 70 strikes and at least 235 dead the same day (AIR).

At least 22 people survived an initial strike but were hit again or died at sea; only three survivors are known to have been rescued, two from a semi-submersible in Oct 2025 and one handed to Costa Rica in Mar 2026 (CBS via Airwars).
First strike, 2 Sep 2025, off Sucre state, Venezuela: 11 killed, including two survivors killed in a follow-on 'double tap' strike reported by the Washington Post and confirmed by the administration.

Peak naval force: Gerald R. Ford carrier strike group, 6 destroyers, 1 cruiser, 1 amphibious assault ship, 2 amphibious transport docks, 1 national security cutter, 1 nuclear attack submarine, about 15,000 personnel (Wikipedia, Operation Southern Spear).

Air assets: AC-130J gunship, P-8A Poseidon and C-40 in El Salvador from mid-Oct 2025; B-52 flights near the Venezuelan coast on 20 Nov 2025; EA-18G Growlers and F-35s in Puerto Rico from Dec 2025; F-35As seen at Roosevelt Roads after the raid.
Surveillance: Saildrone uncrewed surface vessels and a radar installed in Trinidad and Tobago in late Nov 2025; RQ-170 Sentinel stealth drone supported the Maduro raid.
Absolute Resolve timing: execute order 22:46 EST on 2 Jan; assault force at Maduro's compound 01:01 EST (02:01 Caracas); force over water with captives 03:29 EST (DefenseScoop).

Absolute Resolve package: more than 150 aircraft from 20 land and sea bases, including F-22A, F-35A/C, F/A-18E/F, EA-18G, E-2D, B-1B, MH-47G and MH-60M DAP helicopters, plus Space Command and Cyber Command effects; reportedly the first US operational use of one-way attack drones.

Targets on 3 Jan 2026: La Carlota air base, Fuerte Tiuna, Higuerote airport (a Buk-M2E surface-to-air missile system destroyed), La Guaira port (at least five warehouses destroyed) and telecom antennas; Venezuela blamed AGM-154 glide bombs for damage to the IVIC research institute.
One US helicopter was hit by ground fire during the raid but stayed flyable; 7 US personnel were wounded by gunfire and shrapnel.
Designations: Cartel de los Soles terrorist designation (Nov 2025); Clan del Golfo Foreign Terrorist Organization (16 Dec 2025); fentanyl declared a weapon of mass destruction (15 Dec 2025).
Ten oil tankers boarded or seized by mid-2026 as part of the pressure campaign (Wikipedia, Operation Southern Spear).
Cost: at least 4.7 billion US dollars from Aug 2025 to Mar 2026 (Costs of War Project, cited by Wikipedia).

USS Gerald R. Ford left the Caribbean for Operation Epic Fury against Iran in Feb 2026 and returned to Norfolk on 16 May 2026 after a 326-day deployment, the longest since Vietnam (TWZ; Stars and Stripes).
casualties: Boat strikes: 238 killed in 79 strikes, 2 Sep 2025 to 5 Oct 2026 (InSight Crime, 5 Oct 2026); AP-based tally at least 235 in 70 strikes (AIR, 5 Oct 2026). Maduro raid, 3 Jan 2026: 32 Cuban personnel (Cuban government); 47 Venezuelan military (Defence Minister Padrino López, 16 Jan 2026) or 42 to 43 (independent monitors, 6 to 7 Jan); at least 2 civilians; about 75 total per US government assessments reported by the Washington Post (6 Jan 2026); Interior Minister Cabello claimed 100, unverified. US: 7 wounded, no combat deaths; one non-combat death during Southern Spear. Figures for the boat strikes rest mostly on US statements, and the identities of most of the dead are unknown.
displaced: No significant displacement attributed to the campaign in the sources consulted.

timeline.event: First US strike on an alleged drug boat off Venezuela kills 11, including two survivors hit by a follow-on strike.
Administration notifies Congress of a 'non-international armed conflict' with designated cartels.
USS Gerald R. Ford leaves the Mediterranean for US Southern Command; it reaches the Caribbean in mid-November.
Dominican Republic authorizes US access to San Isidro air base and Las Americas airport.
US designates the Clan del Golfo a Foreign Terrorist Organization, a day after declaring fentanyl a weapon of mass destruction.
US announces its first land strike, a CIA drone attack on a Venezuelan port, with no reported casualties.
Operation Absolute Resolve: Maduro and Cilia Flores captured in Caracas and flown to New York.
Delcy Rodríguez sworn in as acting president; Maduro pleads not guilty in New York.
US and Venezuela restore diplomatic relations; the US embassy reopens on 30 March.
USS Gerald R. Ford returns to Norfolk after 326 days, having left the Caribbean for the Iran campaign in February.
AP reports the boat-strike death toll has reached at least 199.
Trump announces a US strike in Venezuela, coordinated with Venezuelan intelligence, that killed Tren de Aragua leader 'Niño Guerrero'.
Rodríguez promises elections at the UN General Assembly but gives no date.
Strike on a boat in the Caribbean kills four, bringing the toll to about 238 in 79 strikes.

outlook: Watch whether strikes keep their current tempo now that the Venezuelan government cooperates, whether courts or Congress constrain the 'armed conflict' legal theory, and whether the model of joint strikes with partner governments, already used in Ecuador and Venezuela, extends to Colombia under President de la Espriella. Maduro's trial and any Venezuelan election timetable will shape whether US forces return to a larger posture.

battles.name: US strike on Tren de Aragua leader 'Niño Guerrero'
battles.place: Tren de Aragua compound, Venezuela (exact location not disclosed)
sides: United States (Southern Command) with Venezuelan intelligence support
battles.outcome: Tren de Aragua leader 'Niño Guerrero' killed; announced by Trump on 12 Jun 2026, with Hegseth saying the strike took place earlier that week.
battles.forces: SOUTHCOM 'kinetic strike'; platform not disclosed; Venezuela provided intelligence and 'specialised technological support'. Marker placed at an approximate central point in Venezuela because the location was not disclosed.
battles.losses: Niño Guerrero killed; other casualties not reported (The Week, 13 Jun 2026).
battles.significance: First publicized joint US-Venezuelan lethal operation, showing how far relations changed after Maduro's capture.

sources.label: The Week: Niño Guerrero killed in US strike (13 Jun 2026)

battles.name: Operation Absolute Resolve (capture of Nicolás Maduro)
battles.place: Fuerte Tiuna and wider Caracas, with strikes at La Carlota, Higuerote and La Guaira, Venezuela
sides: Venezuelan armed forces and Cuban security personnel
battles.outcome: US victory: Maduro and Cilia Flores captured and flown to New York; Delcy Rodríguez became acting president and later cooperated with Washington.
battles.forces: More than 150 aircraft and drones from 20 land and sea bases: F-22A, F-35A/C, F/A-18E/F, EA-18G, E-2D, B-1B, RQ-170, one-way attack drones; Delta Force inserted by 160th SOAR MH-47G and MH-60M; FBI Hostage Rescue Team; Space and Cyber Command effects; USS Iwo Jima received the captives.
battles.losses: Venezuela: 47 military dead (Defence Minister, 16 Jan 2026) or 42 to 43 (independent monitors); Cuba: 32 dead (Cuban government); at least 2 civilians; about 75 total per US assessments (Washington Post via Espreso). US: 7 wounded, none killed; one helicopter damaged.
battles.significance: Removed Maduro by force after months of pressure, reoriented Venezuela toward Washington and opened its oil sector; it also showed the reach of US special operations and suppression of air defences against a state military.

battles.name: US strikes on alleged drug boats in the eastern Pacific
battles.place: International waters of the eastern Pacific, off Colombia, Ecuador and Central America
sides: Crews of alleged drug-smuggling boats and semi-submersibles
battles.outcome: Ongoing; since late October 2025 most strikes in the campaign have taken place in the eastern Pacific (InSight Crime). Start date approximate.
battles.forces: Ships and aircraft of Joint Task Force Southern Spear, with surveillance and maritime patrol aircraft such as the P-8A; individual strike platforms undisclosed. Position approximate.
battles.losses: Majority of the 238 killed in 79 strikes by 5 Oct 2026 (InSight Crime); at least 22 people campaign-wide survived an initial strike but were hit again or died at sea; two survivors of a strike on a semi-submersible were repatriated to Ecuador and Colombia in Oct 2025 (CBS via Airwars).
battles.significance: Shifted the campaign from pressure on Venezuela to a region-wide counter-narcotics strike campaign along cocaine routes from Colombia and Ecuador.

battles.name: US strikes on alleged drug boats in the southern Caribbean
battles.place: International waters of the southern Caribbean, off Venezuela and Trinidad and Tobago
battles.outcome: Ongoing campaign of lethal strikes; the first strikes of Sep 2025 took place here, and strikes resumed here in Sep to Oct 2026, including one on 4 Oct 2026 that killed four.
battles.forces: Ships and aircraft of Joint Task Force Southern Spear; Southcom does not disclose which platform conducts each strike. Position approximate, as Southcom rarely gives locations.
battles.losses: First strike on 2 Sep 2025 killed 11, including two survivors hit by a follow-on strike (CBS News; WaPo via CBS/Airwars); 4 killed on 4 Oct 2026 (AIR). Campaign-wide total: 238 killed in 79 strikes by 5 Oct 2026 (InSight Crime).
battles.significance: Opened a new kind of US military campaign, treating drug smuggling as an armed attack and smugglers as combatants, without congressional authorization; its legality is contested in US courts and by rights groups.
